subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Balanced scales
hotspots.description: The two scales are level — the reactants on one side weigh exactly what the products on the other side weigh. Mass is conserved.
hotspots.positionHint: The two balanced scale arms with molecules on each.
hotspots.function: Shows that product mass equals reactant mass.

hotspots.label: Equal atom counts
hotspots.description: When the count layer is on, every atom splits out and is tallied — the same number of each kind on both sides.
hotspots.positionHint: The split-out atoms with running tallies on each scale.
hotspots.function: Shows the atom counts matching on both sides.

hotspots.label: Atoms rearranged
hotspots.description: The rearrange layer shows the reactant atoms breaking apart and reassembling as products — same atoms, brand-new connections.
hotspots.positionHint: The reactant atoms gliding over to form the products.
hotspots.function: Shows atoms being rearranged, not created.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. Two balanced scales float side by side with molecule groups on each, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Scales: soft warm-gray fixtures; molecules: ball-stick in CPK colors (hydrogen warm off-white, oxygen muted red, carbon soft graphite). Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / molecular-green / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Scale fixtures: soft warm-gray matte, roughness ~0.55. Molecule spheres: CPK colors, roughness ~0.45-0.5. Bond rods: thin graphite cylinders. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: two balanced scales weighing reactants and products, built to be read as 'mass in equals mass out.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: two identical scale fixtures (soft warm-gray, simple base + arm) side by side (spacing ~1.7). LEFT scale pan holds reactant molecules — one O₂ (two muted-red spheres) and one C (soft graphite sphere), a small pile representing the reactants. RIGHT scale pan holds product molecules — one CO₂ ball-stick (graphite center, two muted-red oxygens, double rods). Both arms are level.

2) ATOM COUNT (toggleable layer): each side's molecules split into individual atoms and arrange in a neat row on its pan; the app renders small running tallies that end equal on both sides (C:1 O:2).

3) REARRANGE (toggleable layer): the atoms from the left pan float across and reassemble into the CO₂ on the right pan (app animates the glide), the scales staying level throughout.

Camera: framed so both scales fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 7-11k triangles. Named nodes: Scale_Left, Scale_Right, Pan_Reactants, Pan_Products, Reactant_O2, Reactant_C, Product_CO2, AtomRows, RearrangeTrails, TallyGlow. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
